grammar.title: Verb + -ing or To-Infinitive (want to, enjoy -ing)
grammar.explanation:
When one verb follows another, the second verb is either **to + verb** or **verb-ing**. The first verb decides the form, so you must learn the groups.

Some verbs take **to + verb**: **want**, **decide**, **hope**, **plan**, **learn**, **promise**, and **need**. For example, I **want to learn** Italian, and we **decided to stay** at home.

Other verbs take **verb-ing**: **enjoy**, **finish**, **don't mind**, **can't stand**, **practise**, and **keep**. For example, I **enjoy cooking** for my friends, and have you **finished eating**?

A few verbs, like **like**, **love**, **hate**, **start**, and **continue**, take both forms with the same meaning. It started **to rain** and it started **raining** mean the same thing.

But after **would like**, **would love**, and **would prefer**, always use **to**. Say I'd love **to come**, not I'd love coming.

To make a negative, put **not** before **to** or **-ing**. I decided **not to go**, and I enjoy **not having** to get up early.

After a preposition, always use **-ing**. I'm good **at cooking**, thanks **for helping**, and she's interested **in learning** Spanish. My advice is to do homework daily, and at least try to enjoy doing it.

practice.q: Rewrite using the correct form: I want (learn) Spanish, and I do a course every week.
practice.a: I want to learn Spanish, and I do a course every week.

practice.q: Rewrite using the correct form: She enjoys (do) her homework daily.
practice.a: She enjoys doing her homework daily.

practice.q: Fix the mistake: I enjoy to read the daily newspaper.
practice.a: I enjoy reading the daily newspaper.

practice.q: Fix the mistake: Have you finished to do your homework?
practice.a: Have you finished doing your homework?
